dedupe_keys.name: u s minor high tide flooding

description: U.S. Minor High Tide Flooding is a dataset listed in FEMA Disaster Resilience Hub, a disaster resilience data hub, published or maintained by National Climate Resilience. Annual occurrences of tidal flooding (exceeding local thresholds for minor impacts to infrastructure) have increased 5- to 10-fold since the 1960s in several U.S. coastal cities. The changes in high tide flooding over time are greatest where elevation is lower, local RSL rise is higher, or extreme variability is less. Coverage: United States. The hub lists this as a dataset of National Climate Resilience. Its keywords are High Tide Flooding, Sunny Day Flooding, Minor High Tide Flooding, Nuisance Flooding, Coastal Flooding. The bounding box given is -170.8986,-14.4246,145.8329,49.0034. The hub shows 2022-12-01 as the last modification. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support network, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-fema-resilience-hub.
